fatal_errors: The proposed Guo et al. descriptor method is a phase-prediction framework, whereas the target intervention is high-energy ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering.
No milling or sintering parameters are reconstructed, including milling time, speed, ball-to-powder ratio, atmosphere, SPS temperature, heating rate, or hold time.
A calculation of thermodynamic and empirical descriptors does not itself refine grains, densify a powder compact, or improve mechanical properties.
The cited evidence supports calculating phase-related descriptors but does not support the claimed improvement of microstructure or mechanical properties.
The proposed comparison is operationally ill-defined because it treats a predictive calculation as though it were a physical processing treatment.
explanation: The hypothesis is broadly related to high-entropy-alloy phase stability, and configurational entropy can contribute to phase prediction, but it does not reconstruct the experimentally relevant HEBM-plus-SPS method. It omits the CoCrFeNiTi powder state, processing window, nanocrystalline refinement, densification, FCC/BCC phase fractions, and quantitative hardness and strength outcomes. Its evidence only establishes that the Guo method calculates ΔSmix, δ, Δχ, and VEC; it does not demonstrate microstructure refinement or property optimization. The falsification experiment lacks specified alloys, processing conditions, quantitative endpoints, and phase or microstructure measurements, so it cannot cleanly test the central claim.
